Daily Devotional

December 11

5 So also Christ glorified not himself to be made an high priest; but he that said unto him, Thou art my Son, to day have I begotten thee. 6 As he saith also in another place, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec. (Hebrews 5:5-6 KJV)

Jesus didn’t make Himself a high priest, but was chosen and ordained by God to be our high priest. The verse saying “to day have I begotten thee” is a quote from Psalms (Psalms 2:7), and is also quoted in Acts (Acts 13:33), and is not talking about the birth of Jesus, but the resurrection, as that is when Jesus became our high priest. Just think we have a high priest at the right hand of the Father, to intercede for us when we need Him to. How could we have a better high priest than the very Son of God, to plead our case before His Father? With His own Son pleading our case, you know that God will hear our defense, and forgive us of all our trespasses. Wow, that is amazing.

Jesus is not a high priest according to the law, as He is not of the lineage of Aaron, but His priesthood predates the law, and is after the order of Melchisedec, who was the King of Salem, and high priest in the time of Abraham. So Jesus is before and superior to the priests that were created under the law brought by Moses. Since Jesus is of a different priesthood, then He must bring a new Covenant to operate under, and it is completely different than the Old Covenant. This further illustrates why you can’t mix the Old Testament law with the New Testament Grace (Romans 11:6) that Jesus brought to us, as the two are of completely different linage. Our churches have tried to mix the law mentality with grace, and the two just don’t mix (Matthew 9:17). Understand that the Grace of God saves us, and it has nothing to do with our actions, but only to do with our accepting Jesus as our Savior, and making Him our Lord. Thank you Jesus for bringing us salvation by grace.

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
